rejected.title: Parliament and the courts
card: Parliament makes most laws. These laws are called statutes, or Acts of Parliament. Parliament can make new laws and change or repeal old ones.
Courts apply the law to the cases that come before them. A judge or magistrate decides what the law means for the facts of that case.
Precedent
when a higher court, such as the Supreme Court, decides a case, its reasons can become a rule that later courts follow in similar cases. Higher courts bind lower courts in the same hierarchy.
Statutory interpretation
when the words of an Act are unclear in a case, a court works out what they mean. If a higher court does this, its reading can guide how the Act is applied later.
rejected.remember: Parliament makes most laws. Courts apply them and also shape law through precedent and interpretation.

a.q: Which of these is a court making law, rather than only applying it?
opts: Explaining what an unclear word in an Act means
Passing a new Act to cover a gap in the law
Repealing an Act that is out of date
Voting on a bill in the Legislative Assembly
a.why: When a court explains what an unclear word in an Act means, its reading can guide later cases, so it shapes the law. The other three are things parliament does, and the card gives them to parliament, not to courts.
a.clue: Which option is something a court does with the words of an Act?

b.q: A Victorian Act bans "vehicles" from a park. In a Supreme Court case, a judge must decide if an electric scooter is a vehicle, and rules that it is. Which statement best describes what the judge did?
opts: Interpreted the Act, and the ruling can guide later cases
Made a new statute that now replaces the original Act
Repealed the ban because its wording was unclear
Followed a lower court's ruling that bound the judge
b.why: The word "vehicle" was unclear in this case, so the judge worked out its meaning. That is statutory interpretation, and because the Supreme Court is a higher court, the reading can guide later cases. The judge did not make a statute, because parliament makes statutes, and a lower court's ruling cannot bind a higher court.
b.clue: The Act already exists, and one word in it is unclear.

Saying the magistrate's ruling 'can guide later cases', in both the option and the why, misleads Year 11 students on a point VCE tests directly. Use a Supreme Court or County Court judge instead.
